stewart_read: On a recycled lead, the rep proactively supplies the prior rep's name when the customer can't recall it, smoothing an awkward moment and signaling continuity/legitimacy of the follow-up.
coaching_implication: Small but real trust-building move — worth naming as a positive habit to reinforce, especially on recycled leads where customers often can't place who they spoke to.

quote: I don't even know if ION has those, but that's another option I wanted to look at.
stewart_read: Customer asks directly about ground-mount panels. Rep responds immediately and honestly at 02:05 ('we don't do ground mounts') without fumbling, then redirects to what Ion does offer — a clean example of admit-and-recover knowledge-gap handling.
coaching_implication: Positive example to hold up: don't dodge, don't fabricate, state the limitation plainly and pivot to value. Worth using as a coaching model for other reps who over-explain or guess on capability questions.

quote: Say that again. So when you say roll solar and roof, do you mean, like, roof shingles or panels on the roof?
stewart_read: The rep answers the customer's direct clarifying question accurately (02:41) but treats it as a definitional Q&A rather than tying the bundle back to the customer's stated HELOC/roof-timing constraint as the reason to act now.
alternative_hypothesis: This is not a curiosity-creation failure — the customer asked a direct question and deserved a direct answer, which the rep gave. The miss is narrower: no flip connecting the bundle to the customer's own timeline urgency.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop with something like tying the bundle answer back to the HELOC/roof timeline ('that's exactly why doing them together makes sense given your roof timing') rather than leaving the answer purely definitional.

quote: Oh, okay. You just haven't gotten that over to us yet?
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior unresolved commitment (bill promised to Meg, not yet sent) and cites being busy. Rep confirms the gap but doesn't probe further into why or what would make it easier this time.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be intentional pacing — pressing harder here risked friction with a customer who just said he's not in a rush, and the rep instead moved to book the appointment first, which is a defensible sequencing choice.
coaching_implication: This is operator judgment, not a hard schema violation — flag as an area to test (asking one clarifying question about the delay) but note the rep's choice to prioritize booking first is reasonable given the customer's stated low urgency.

quote: And a lot of people are able to bundle the two and save money, and there is tax incentives for doing solar. So it's making sense for a lot of people to combine the roof and the solar cost together.
stewart_read: The rep does bridge to the roofing cross-sell correctly and quickly once the customer mentions needing a new roof — this is the positive execution of the schema's bridge pattern, not a miss.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model bridge: customer states roof need, rep pivots to bundled roof+solar estimate within seconds, matching the SESSION18_fcbf33c1 positive example in the schema.

quote: Once you get me that, though, I'll put you in for 09:30 tomorrow, spot you out for an hour, and they'll give you a roof estimate as well as a solar estimate.
stewart_read: The appointment is explicitly conditioned on the customer sending the bill, which he has not yet done by end of call. There is no button-up handshake ('is that fair?'), no explicit day-of-week stated, and no text-confirmation promise.
coaching_implication: Flag this as fragile: without the bill and without a locked handshake, this slot is at real risk of evaporating. Coach the rep to still deliver full button-up mechanics even on a conditional booking so the customer has a concrete commitment to hold onto regardless of bill timing.

quote: Alright. Appreciate it, Cutter. K. Of course. Look forward to hearing back from you.
stewart_read: Call ends with a passive close ('look forward to hearing back from you') rather than a confirmed handshake or stated next step owned by the rep — no recap of day/time, no text-confirmation promise, no 'is that fair?' check.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always close with the full button-up sequence — restate day/time, mention the one-hour block, promise a text confirmation — even when the booking is conditional on an outstanding item like the bill.
